input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 grants only for-cause, insolvency and security/SLA/legal-violation termination rights (9.1–9.3), and Section 8.1 fixes a three-year term with Section 2.1 expressly negating any reduction or termination right. Non-renewal (8.2) and force-majeure exit (27.3) are not convenience rights. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory, so we add a 30-day convenience right (new 9.4) and confirm Vendor has no convenience right; Section 10.2 already refunds prepaid recurring Fees for the post-termination period, so no refund language is added. We also conform Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay commitment does not contradict the new right.

proposal.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice; bar Vendor convenience termination; conform take-or-pay clause
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a convenience exit: new Section 9.4 lets us terminate the Agreement or an Order Form on thirty days' written notice and confirms Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term, and we conform Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay commitment no longer denies that right. Prepaid fees are already refunded under Section 10.2.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

ops.newText: , subject to Customer's termination rights under this Agreement.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
